messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High GPU queue growth detected in prod-us-west (~230% over baseline) — autoscaler failed to add capacity (scaleup_attempts=3, last_error=scale_limit). Paging oncall: @sara (oncall)

sara (oncall): saw it, joining. can someone drop recent autoscaler logs?

daniel (eng-sre): past 10m median latency spiked from 120ms -> 850ms. queue length jumped from 400 -> 2.6k. autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale_limit' returned by cloud provider when requesting GPUs. also some 429s from provider control-plane.

maya (infra): provider reports region quota limits for GPU SKU in us-west-2. support ticket opened (INC-7832). looks like our fallback pools in us-east are healthy.

sara (oncall): short term mitigation: enable cross-region routing to us-east-1 for non-data-local tenants and increase eviction aggressiveness on low-priority queues. can we flip routing?

daniel (eng-sre): routing switch is ready as a config flag. pushing change to route.non_critical -> us-east-1. will follow with a canary on 5% of traffic.

kevin (customer-ops): any ETA on when we can stop throttling customers? customers seeing 503s for generation requests. we have 3 customers in S1 experiencing degraded SLAs.

sara (oncall): will do customer impact summary in 10m. priority orders: safety/enterprise customers get preserved capacity, see if we can warm dedicated-pools.

daniel (eng-sre): canary flip in 30s. pushing: 
```json
{ "route": "non_critical", "target_region": "us-east-1", "canary_pct": 5 }
```

incident-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started by @daniel (eng-sre) — 5% -> healthy. metrics: queue in us-east canary down 40%.

sara (oncall): ok proceed to 25% if stable for next 2 mins. also start eviction for non-paying free-tier jobs (policy low-pri).

leah (product): flag: customers using Dedicated capacity should not be affected by cross-region routing. verify their routing policies.

maya (infra): confirmed: dedicated pools pinned to region; not impacted by this routing change.

kevin (customer-ops): told affected customers we have degraded perf and are redirecting some work to alternate pools; two asked for ETA and offered temporary higher-priority tokens — applied to one tenant.

daniel (eng-sre): after 2m canary looks good. increasing to 25%. queue length overall dropping ~60%. provider 429s still seen for new allocations.

sara (oncall): while routing mitigates incoming traffic, we need to address longer-term: autoscaler retries exhausted due to provider scale limits, and our operator used naive backoff. opening live-incident task: investigate autoscaler backoff + fallback to cold-pool warmup.

maya (infra): started background warmup on spare instances in us-east dedicated pool (cold-pool warmup ID cw-992). this will take ~8-12m to be fully ready.

incident-bot: noted major incident severity P1 -> paging escalation to eng-sre leads.

leah (product): any customer data loss?

sara (oncall): no persisted data loss, only increased latency and some 503s. no model state affected.

kevin (customer-ops): updating status page: "Degraded performance for generation endpoints in US-WEST. We're routing some traffic to alternate pools while we resolve GPU provisioning limits."

maya (infra): provider updated support ticket: quota expansions delayed due to capacity constraints; they suggested using alternative instance family (a100->a10x) — cost/latency tradeoff.

daniel (eng-sre): we can temporarily spin alternative GPU types but runtime kernel selection needs recompile for correct quantization path. I can trigger a hot-compat mode that supports a10x but with 15-25% slower throughput.

sara (oncall): do it if warmup will finish slower than traffic needs. prioritize reducing customer 503s.

leah (product): estimate customer impact window if we do hot-compat: ~20m ramp + 10m stabilization. better than ongoing 503s.

kevin (customer-ops): sending an update to effected customers: ETA ~30–40m to full mitigation.

maya (infra): starting hot-compat spin-up on alternative SKUs in us-west to avoid cross-region latency for enterprise tenants that do not allow cross-region: launching with reduced batch sizes.

incident-bot: deployment events: hot-compat infra tasks initiated by @maya (infra).

daniel (eng-sre): note: autoscaler code also needs a safety check: if provider returns 'scale_limit' we currently stop attempts for 15m. propose exponential retry with jitter and fallback to pre-warmed cold pools.

sara (oncall): agreed — add action item.

maya (infra): warmup completed for some alt SKUs; traffic shifting shows enterprise pools stable. overall 503s dropped by 90%. queue lengths trending toward normal.

kevin (customer-ops): customers acknowledging updates, one enterprise thank-you.

leah (product): postmortem outline: root cause (region GPU exhaustion + autoscaler retry policy + provider 429s), mitigations (cross-region routing, hot-compat alternative SKUs, eviction of low-pri), action items (autoscaler change, pre-warm cold-pools, add provider capacity alarms, update runbook).

sara (oncall): starting oncall handoff notes for tomorrow: timeline, mitigations, outstanding provider ticket. assigning owners now.

- daniel (eng-sre): owner for autoscaler code change (PR + test)
- maya (infra): owner for cold-pool prewarm and hot-compat templates
- kevin (customer-ops): owner for customer comms and status updates
- leah (product): owner for postmortem write-up and SLA impact assessment

sara (oncall): final status: incident moving from mitigated -> monitoring. will keep thread open until provider confirms quota change or we have long-term mitigations shipped. thanks all — great cross-team moves. :purple_heart:

incident-bot: incident cleared to severity P2 (monitoring). metrics to watch: queue_length.prod_us_west, autoscaler_errors.scale_limit, provider_429_rate, cold_pool_ready_pct.

leah (product): one more note — add a customer-facing timeline for the postmortem.

sara (oncall): noted. action items logged in ops board: OPS-1122, OPS-1123, OPS-1124. closing live bridge.

daniel (eng-sre): quick follow-up: I'll open a draft PR for autoscaler retry logic and link it to OPS-1122.

maya (infra): prepping cloud-provider fallback templates and cost estimates for hot-compat (OPS-1123).

kevin (customer-ops): drafting customer note for postmortem, linking to status page updates (OPS-1124).

sara (oncall): thanks everyone. handoff to next oncall in morning. if anything regresses wake me.
